```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE,
  fig.width=9, fig.height=4.2, dpi=160)
```

L0glm's shrinking active set, compiled solvers and fast GIC preset can deliver
striking gains in both speed and support recovery. These examples compare
complete fitting and selection workflows, with the tuning rule stated for every
method. The realistic deconvolution examples are generated by the
[website benchmark](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/L0glm/blob/master/benchmarks/benchmark_website_examples.R).
The [README benchmark](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/L0glm/blob/master/README.Rmd)
also reproduces the million-predictor LASSO comparisons.

## One million predictor example

The design has 500 observations, one million standard-normal predictors and
60 nonzero coefficients of either sign. L0glm uses GIC-preset ISIS plus a relaxed
refit. LASSO and fully relaxed LASSO are tuned by BIC or five-fold CV.

| Method | Selection | Seconds | GIC | TP | FP | FN | TN | F1 | MCC |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **L0glm + ISIS** | GIC preset | **3.49** | **2583** | **40** | **3** | 20 | 999937 | **0.777** | **0.787** |
| LASSO | BIC path | 22.75 | 14789 | 23 | 612 | 37 | 999328 | 0.066 | 0.118 |
| Relaxed LASSO | BIC path | 21.42 | 10588 | 21 | 453 | 39 | 999487 | 0.079 | 0.124 |
| LASSO | 5-fold CV | 123.13 | 4309 | 17 | 50 | 43 | 999890 | 0.268 | 0.268 |
| Relaxed LASSO | 5-fold CV | 91.76 | 7413 | 20 | 252 | 40 | 999688 | 0.120 | 0.156 |

```{r million-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=4.2, dev.args=list(pointsize=18), fig.cap="Fast fitting and selection, higher sensitivity and fewer false positives in the million-predictor example. L0glm uses a GIC preset; both LASSO methods use five-fold CV. There are 60 true effects."}
layout(matrix(1:3, nrow=1), widths=c(1.3, 1, 1))
par(mar=c(4, 6.5, 2.8, 1), mgp=c(2.5, .6, 0), family="sans", cex.axis=.85,
  bg="white", col.axis="#34465d", col.lab="#34465d", col.main="#0a1930")
labels <- c("L0glm + ISIS", "LASSO", "Relaxed LASSO")
cols <- c("#087e83", "#8b5cc7", "#d04a78")
seconds <- c(3.49, 123.13, 91.76)
plot(seconds, 3:1, log="x", xlim=c(1, 220), ylim=c(.6, 3.4), pch=21, bg=cols,
  col=cols, cex=2.2, yaxt="n", xlab="Seconds (log scale)", ylab="", bty="n")
axis(2, at=3:1, labels=labels, las=1, tick=FALSE, cex.axis=.9)
abline(v=c(1, 10, 100), col="#e1ebef", lty=3)
points(seconds, 3:1, pch=21, bg=cols, col=cols, cex=2.2)
text(seconds, 3:1, sprintf("%.2f s", seconds), pos=ifelse(seconds > 50, 2, 4),
  offset=.8, cex=.8, col="#29455a")
title("Fast fitting and selection", adj=0, cex.main=1.1)
par(mar=c(4, 1, 2.8, 1))
tp <- c(40, 17, 20)
plot(tp, 3:1, xlim=c(0, 60), ylim=c(.6, 3.4), pch=21, bg=cols, col=cols,
  cex=2.2, yaxt="n", xlab="True positives (of 60)", ylab="", bty="n")
text(tp+2, 3:1, tp, pos=4, cex=.9, col="#29455a")
title("Higher sensitivity", adj=0, cex.main=1.1)
fp <- c(3, 50, 252)
plot(fp, 3:1, xlim=c(0, 310), ylim=c(.6, 3.4), pch=21, bg=cols, col=cols,
  cex=2.2, yaxt="n", xlab="False positives", ylab="", bty="n")
text(fp+9, 3:1, fp, pos=4, cex=.9, col="#29455a")
title("Fewer false positives", adj=0, cex.main=1.1)
layout(1)
```

In this simulation L0glm is **35 times faster than five-fold-CV LASSO** and
recovers more true effects with fewer false positives. The L0glm timing includes
screening and one preset fit; the other methods evaluate up to 40 native path
values, with paths refitted in each CV training fold. BIC is shown alongside CV
because GIC can select a null LASSO model at this dimension. All rows retain GIC
as a common evaluation score. Five-fold comparisons use the same random folds.

Simulation is excluded from timings. The documented run uses one BLAS thread
and eight screening threads; the design is held in memory. The L0glm time is
the median of three runs. The common-scoring CV implementation used for the
LASSO rows evaluates folds serially. Standalone benchmarks that call
`cv.glmnet()` use parallel folds through `cv_glmnet_parallel()`.
See the
[million-predictor tutorial](high-dimensional.html) for the complete data setup.

## Single channel deconvolution

A realistic blurred Poisson spike train has **10,000 observations, 10,000
predictors and 1,000 true peaks**. Every fit is evaluated using the original
Poisson likelihood and a common GIC.

<!-- BEGIN single-metrics -->
| Method | Selection | Seconds | GIC | TP | FP | FN | TN | F1 | MCC |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| L0glm | GIC preset | 0.20 | 102682 | 845 | 154 | 155 | 8846 | 0.845 | 0.828 |
| LASSO | GIC path | 0.40 | 145904 | 950 | 2096 | 50 | 6904 | 0.470 | 0.467 |
| Relaxed LASSO | GIC path | 0.64 | 122083 | 905 | 999 | 95 | 8001 | 0.623 | 0.607 |
| LASSO | 5-fold CV | 4.83 | 146234 | 951 | 2146 | 49 | 6854 | 0.464 | 0.462 |
| Relaxed LASSO | 5-fold CV | 6.70 | 133122 | 920 | 1523 | 80 | 7477 | 0.534 | 0.524 |
<!-- END single-metrics -->

L0glm uses one GIC preset with a relaxed refit. LASSO and relaxed LASSO search
ten explicit lambda values using GIC or five-fold CV, with a weighted-Gaussian
approximation and observation weights `1/(y+0.1)`. CV selects glmnet's minimum
weighted prediction error using four parallel workers. ABESS is omitted from
this large example.
The [deconvolution tutorial](deconvolution.html) shows mirrored signals and
true-versus-estimated coefficient plots.

## Multichannel deconvolution

The GC/MS-style simulation also has **10,000 rows, 10,000 candidate peak
locations and 1,000 true peaks**, with **all 226 informative mass channels**
retained. Shared chromatographic peak times correspond to active coefficient
rows; within-row coefficients describe the mass spectra.

<!-- BEGIN multi-metrics -->
| Method | Selection | Seconds | GIC | TP | FP | FN | TN | F1 | MCC | Within-row F1 | Within-row MCC |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| L0glm | GIC preset | 9.63 | 5615963 | 944 | 11 | 56 | 8989 | 0.966 | 0.962 | 0.909 | 0.864 |
| Group LASSO | GIC path | 244.87 | 7413616 | 980 | 860 | 20 | 8140 | 0.690 | 0.685 | 0.842 | 0.768 |
| Relaxed group LASSO | GIC path | 906.34 | 6138687 | 909 | 309 | 91 | 8691 | 0.820 | 0.802 | 0.853 | 0.782 |
| Group LASSO | 5-fold CV | 813.42 | 9639345 | 998 | 4242 | 2 | 4758 | 0.320 | 0.316 | 0.886 | 0.830 |
| Relaxed group LASSO | 5-fold CV | 3199.62 | 6198648 | 962 | 502 | 38 | 8498 | 0.781 | 0.769 | 0.856 | 0.785 |
<!-- END multi-metrics -->

Row F1 and MCC measure peak recovery. Within-row F1 and MCC assess spectral
sparsity among correctly recovered true-positive peaks. L0glm uses the full
Poisson likelihood with channel-specific working weights. Grouped glmnet
uses shared row weights `1/(rowMeans(y)+0.1)` for its labelled Gaussian
approximation. GIC selection scores ten lambda values using the original
Poisson likelihood; five-fold CV selects the minimum weighted prediction error
on the same lambda grid. Fully relaxed fits use `gamma=0`. L0glm uses
`lambda="gic"` and four outcome-fitting threads; CV uses four parallel workers.
Timings include the complete fitting and selection workflow, including worker
startup for CV. The preset time is the median of three runs with matching
coefficients. Simulation and final metric reporting are excluded.

The [deconvolution tutorial](deconvolution.html) stacks observed data, ground
truth and fitted coefficient heatmaps, and shows all-channel coefficient
comparisons in a single column.

## Native validation and OpenMP

Native validation scoring preserves multichannel OpenMP and returns the same
checkpoint models as the R-validation path. This reproducible test uses
1,000 predictors, 16 channels, 60 active rows and an independent Poisson replicate
for validation. Median times are from five fits, with one BLAS thread.

| Backend | Outcome threads | Seconds | Validation deviance | GIC | F1 | MCC |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| General R | 1 | 1.12 | 0.357612 | 42728.05 | 0.944882 | 0.942790 |
| Native | 1 | 0.08 | 0.357612 | 42728.05 | 0.944882 | 0.942790 |
| Native | 2 | 0.06 | 0.357612 | 42728.05 | 0.944882 | 0.942790 |
| Native | 4 | 0.04 | 0.357612 | 42728.05 | 0.944882 | 0.942790 |
| Native | 8 | 0.04 | 0.357612 | 42728.05 | 0.944882 | 0.942790 |

Run [benchmark_native_validation.R](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/L0glm/blob/master/benchmarks/benchmark_native_validation.R)
to reproduce this comparison. Results agree across thread counts; validation
predictors are shared across workers. Paired 10,000-predictor tests also preserve
the unvalidated fit, with 16-channel timing 0.874 s versus 0.878 s.

## Reproduce and extend

* [README benchmark source](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/L0glm/blob/master/README.Rmd): data generation, comparisons and plots.
* [Solver/problem-size benchmark](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/L0glm/blob/master/benchmarks/1_benchmarks_L0glm_solvers_problem_sizes.R): solvers, families, matrix storage and sizes.
* [Single/multichannel benchmark](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/L0glm/blob/master/benchmarks/2_benchmarks_L0glm_single_and_multichannel_vs_other_methods.R): detailed signal examples and alternative methods.
* [`sparseglm()`](../reference/sparseglm.html): use the same comparison framework on your own data.

The benchmarks were run on an **HP ZBook Fury 17.3-inch G8 Mobile Workstation**
with an **11th-generation Intel Core i9-11950H at 2.60 GHz**, **8 physical cores
and 16 logical cores**, running Windows and R 4.5.0 with OpenBLAS. BLAS uses one
thread. Screening in the million-predictor example uses eight physical cores.
Multichannel deconvolution uses four outcome-fitting threads, and deconvolution
CV uses four parallel workers. Single-channel fits use one fitting thread.
Timings will vary with hardware and tuning choices. F1 and MCC evaluate the known simulated
support; it is never used to select models. Likelihood floors and approximation
labels are explicit in the benchmark source.
